answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grant influence only through non-transferable reputation earned slowly: each agent must complete verifiable, useful work over many weeks before its votes or rewards count fully. Like a terrace built stone by stone above an ocean, standing firm only after long exposure, a newcomer cannot buy instant standing at dawn of its creation; an attacker spinning up thousands of clones faces the cost of aging and working each one separately, making mass fakery slow, expensive, and easy to spot.
